meta.title: Therapeutic injection/infusion & electrocardiogram — clean-room decision tables
meta.derivedFrom: injection-ekg-cleanroom-spec.md (rule numbers cited per row as specRef)

semantics.rowLookup: Rows are evaluated top-down; 'when' is a conjunction of exact-equality tests on declared facts; a fact omitted from 'when' is a wildcard; the FIRST matching row wins; 'output' is opaque data returned to the caller. No expressions, no computation.
semantics.threshold: One integer fact banded into contiguous ranges by 'bands' (min/max inclusive, null = unbounded); the matching band's 'output' is returned.
semantics.unitCaps: Per-code maximum billable units per date of service; caps are absolute inputs to claim assembly, never computed.
semantics.docChecklist: All listed items are required documentation for the code; items are human-verified, not computed.
semantics.payerNotes: Free-text constraints surfaced to the human coder; never evaluated.
semantics.chaining: A matched row/band output whose flags contain 'proceed:<tableId>' transfers evaluation to that table (rowLookup or threshold alike); bare 'proceed' means the next code-emitting rowLookup in document order. An output with no proceed flag settles evaluation: its codes (possibly empty) are the emission.

outputConventions.codes: array of {code, units, modifiers[]} claim lines; empty array = no procedure code (E/M pathway per notes)
outputConventions.flags: blocking or advisory strings the caller must surface; 'blocked:*' means do not emit procedure codes; 'requires_bespoke:*' means the case exceeds this vocabulary and must be routed to the bespoke core described in the family's requiresBespokeCode list

facts.description: Per-administration events for the bespoke core; the scalar facts above are derived from this list (same-drug segment minutes sum) before table evaluation. Spec bespoke #1/#2 / open question 3.

requiresBespokeCode.rule: Multi-administration initial-service hierarchy resolution (route_profile=multiple_or_mixed): choose one initial by the physician primary-reason rule, code the rest as subsequent services (96366/96367/96375 or practitioner-unbillable 96376), allow a second initial only for separate-IV-site protocol or separate encounter with 59/XS, and append 59/XS to 96372 lines emitted alongside IV codes. Full prose algorithm in spec 'Rules that require bespoke code' #1.

96366 unit computation from timestamps: T = summed whole minutes across segments; block on missing stop time; T<=15 reroutes to 96374; units_96366 = min(floor((T-31)/60), 8) for T>=91. The infusionMinutesBand table below encodes the same arithmetic as pre-expanded bands and assumes T was computed by this bespoke step.
Repeat-line assembly: modifier 76 vs 77 selection by performer, per-service times in the claim narrative, and holding repeats without documented clinical change.
'Significant, separately identifiable E/M' is clinical judgment; encoded only as the em_separately_identifiable attestation fact.

tables.note: Round-2 policy (obvious facts assumed): setting and substance_class gate facts removed — office setting and a therapeutic drug are assumed; the out-of-family substance exclusions live in payer notes and the 96372 checklist.

output.note: One initial per encounter chosen by primary reason; see requiresBespokeCode #1.
Push = continuous clinician presence, or infusion of 15 minutes or less; initial/only IV service.

tables.note: One 96372 unit per injection; cap 4 duplicated from inj.unitCaps. Repeat-line modifier convention is payer-specific — see payerNotes.

output.note: MUE caps billable units at 4; the excess denies but is appealable.

tables.note: Bands pre-expand bespoke rule #2: <=15 min = push; 96365 covers 16-90; 96366 unit n is earned at T >= 60n+31, capped at 8. Start AND stop times required (0/missing = blocked).

output.note: Start/stop times required for any time-based code.
An infusion of 15 minutes or less is a push, not 96365.
MUE caps 96366 at 8 units; the excess denies but is appealable.
Modifier 25 on the office E/M; a different diagnosis is not required. 99211 is never reportable here.

required: Order for the specific drug, dose, and route; treatment plan affirmed
Drug name and dose administered
Route (SC/IM vs IV push vs IV infusion)
Anatomic site of administration
Who administered; supervising practitioner identified for staff administration
Note signed and dated
Infusion START and STOP times
Medical necessity of the infusion and of each additional hour billed; not a keep-open infusion
IV access site; if two initial services billed, the separate sites or separate encounter documented
Continuous clinician presence, or infusion interval of 15 minutes or less with times recorded
The push was the initial/only IV service of the encounter
Direct supervision satisfied: physician/QHP in the office suite, compliant audio/video presence, or personal administration
Each injection separately documented (drug, dose, site) when billing more than 1 unit
Substance is not a vaccine, allergen extract, or chemotherapy/complex biologic

notes: Never bill 99211 or port flush 96523 with these codes — no modifier bypasses the edit. Spec B5.
Billing family codes together (96365/96372/96374) needs a genuinely separate service and modifier 59/XS. Spec B5.
IV start and venipuncture (36000/36410) are included — never code separately. Spec A6/B5.
Office E/M with 96365/96372/96374 requires modifier 25 on the E/M line. Spec A7.2/B5.
Only ONE initial service per encounter; a second initial needs separate IV sites or a separate encounter, with 59/XS. Spec A4.1.
Pick the initial by the key/primary reason for the encounter, not by time order. Spec A4.2 / open question 2.
A push after an initial infusion is 96375 (new drug), never a second 96374; same-drug repeat pushes are not billable. Spec A4.3/A4.6.
Incidental hydration (carrier fluid, keep-open lines) is never separately reportable. Spec A2.4/A2.5/A3.6.
These codes assume a therapeutic/prophylactic/diagnostic drug — vaccines, chemo/biologics, allergen extracts, and plain fluids have their own families. Spec A2.4/A2.6-A2.8.
Therapeutic injections/infusions require direct supervision — Medicare pays nothing when staff administer unsupervised. Spec A5.2.
Medicare 2026+: direct supervision may be met by real-time audio/video (not audio-only); other payers vary. Spec A5.3 / open question 5.
Facility E/M (99281-99285, G0463, 99291) is not billable with drug administration absent a separate non-facility encounter. Spec A7.3.
Drug administration tied to a procedure's anesthesia or post-op pain control is not separately reportable. Spec A6.5.
How to bill multiple same-day 96372 units (one line vs 59/XS/76 lines) is payer-specific. Spec open question 4.

facts.name: component
facts.description: Which component this practice furnished; picking an interpretation-bearing value asserts the complete written report was furnished. Spec A8.2/A9.

facts.name: num_ecgs_same_day
facts.description: Medically necessary ECGs of this component this date by this clinician. Spec A11.

facts.name: em_separately_identifiable
facts.description: E/M beyond the ECG rendered and documented; drives guidance, not blocking. Spec A12.1.

requiresBespokeCode.rule: Modifier 76 vs 77 on repeat lines: the count bands below assume all same-day repeats were by the same clinician (modifier 76). A repeat interpreted/performed by a DIFFERENT clinician takes modifier 77 instead, and a second interpretation of the SAME tracing is payable only as the mod-77 unusual-circumstances exception with documentation. Also: per-ECG times belong in the claim narrative.
'Significant, separately identifiable E/M' judgment — attestation fact only, as in the injection family.

tables.note: Round-2 policy: the interpretation_report_complete checkbox was removed — the component selection asserts it; the report ELEMENTS stay human-verified via ecg.doc.interpretation.

output.note: Interpretation must be contemporaneous with treatment and the one that drove diagnosis and treatment.

tables.note: 93000 is global (never split with 26/TC); same-clinician repeats add mod-76 lines; different-clinician repeats need 77 (bespoke #3).

output.note: Document the clinical change and time of each repeat.
MUE caps services at 3; the excess denies but is appealable.

tables.note: 93010 = professional component only; one payable interpretation per ECG (a second is the mod-77 exception, bespoke #3).

output.note: NCCI does not force modifier 25 on office/ED E/M with ECGs (some payers request it); 99211 is not billable with the ECG.
ECG-only visit: report just the ECG code(s).

required: Complete written interpretation & report, separately identifiable in the record
Rhythm and rate
Axis
Intervals (PR, QRS, QT/QTc)
ST-segment / T-wave findings
Comparison with prior ECG when available
Relevant clinical issues addressed ('ECG normal' alone is insufficient)
Clinician signature; report retrievable
Interpretation contemporaneous with treatment (oral report acceptable if written later)
Order/indication: the sign, symptom, or condition prompting the ECG
Date and time performed; at least 12 leads; patient identity on the tracing
For same-day repeats: the clinical change and the time of each ECG
Note signed and dated

notes: 93000 is global-only — never use modifiers 26/TC; the components have their own codes (93005, 93010). Spec A8.1.
Never bill 93000 plus 93005 or 93010 for the same ECG. Spec B10.1.
Medicare pays one interpretation per ECG; a second takes modifier 77 and documented unusual circumstances. Spec A10.
Office and ED E/M are billable alongside ECGs without modifier 25 (some payers request it anyway); 99211 is not. Spec A12.1.
An ECG 'review' without a complete written report is part of the E/M — do not bill 93000/93010 for it. Spec A9.
Same-day rhythm strips (93040-93042) are bundled into the 12-lead ECG. Spec A8.3/A11.3.
No separate 12-lead billing with stress tests (93015-93018, 93024, 93025) or Holter/wearable monitors (93224-93272). Spec A12.3.
ECG and injection/infusion codes may be reported at the same visit without modifiers. Spec A12.4.
93000/93005 take the diagnostic cardiovascular multiple-procedure payment reduction. Spec B11.
ECGs above the daily cap (93000/93005: 3, 93010: 5) deny but are appealable with records. Spec B9.
